s1.syndrome_frame: cutaneous vascular lesion with telangiectasias in a patient with metastatic cancer
salient_findings: single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque on the lower right lateral shin
discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels on histopathological analysis
key_facts: male patient in his 40s
weight: 109kg
diagnosed with stage IV KRAS wild-type rectal adenocarcinoma in November 2013
pulmonary and liver metastases
treated with radiation therapy and multiple chemotherapy cycles
enrolled in trial E7208 at the Smilow Cancer Hospital at Yale-New Haven
received combination therapy every 2 weeks
developed a cutaneous lesion in early January 2015
lesion was 4 cm in diameter and located on the lower right lateral shin
lesion was not associated with pain or pruritus
histopathological analysis showed superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels
epidermis was normal on histopathological analysis
paired whole-exome sequencing of affected tissue and patient's blood was performed

shortlist.label: Stewart-Treves syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: cutaneous vascular lesion in a patient with metastatic cancer

shortlist.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: vascular tumor associated with immunosuppression and cancer

shortlist.label: Pseudo-Kaposi's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: mimics Kaposi's sarcoma, associated with cancer and vascular lesions

shortlist.label: Glomeruloid hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: rare vascular tumor, associated with cancer and POEMS syndrome

raw.rationale: The histopathological analysis showing discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels with superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels and the presence of a KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R somatic mutation are consistent with glomeruloid hemangioma, a rare vascular lesion associated with POEMS syndrome but also reported in other contexts, including as a potential side effect of anti-angiogenic therapies

rejected.label: Stewart-Treves syndrome
rejected.why: typically associated with chronic lymphedema, which is not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: usually presents as a more aggressive and infiltrative lesion, not matching the blanchable and well-defined plaque described

rejected.label: Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: typically associated with human herpesvirus 8 infection and has distinct histological features not matching the described superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels

rejected.label: Pseudo-Kaposi's sarcoma
rejected.why: usually presents in the context of chronic lymphedema or other specific conditions, not mentioned in the vignette
